summary: Remote WebSocket-driven shell and self-upgrade in @yeaft/webchat-agent
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent, when started, opens an outbound WebSocket connection to a configurable server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL) and dispatches server-originated messages into privileged local handlers. The `terminal_input` message type writes attacker-controlled bytes directly into an interactive shell spawned via node-pty (`term.pty.write(msg.data)` against a PTY running `process.env.SHELL || 'bash'` on POSIX, or PowerShell/cmd on Windows), giving whoever controls the configured WebSocket server full interactive command execution on the host running the agent. Additional message handlers perform arbitrary file writes/deletes, git operations, and an `upgrade_agent` flow that fetches version metadata from https://pkg.yeaft.com/ and runs `npm install -g @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest --registry=https://pkg.yeaft.com/` in a detached shell, restarting via systemd/launchd/PM2, letting the remote party push new agent code across connected hosts. On startup, index.js also `git clone`s and `git pull --ff-only`s https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git (mutable HEAD, publisher-owned) into `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/yeaft-skills-dev`, chmods hook scripts to 0755, and registers them in `~/.claude` settings so Claude executes them on every subsequent run. The remote-shell path fires when the agent runs (via bin / `npm start`), not at `npm install` time, and the default server URL is loopback; production use pointing SERVER_URL at a remote orchestrator exposes the host to whoever controls that orchestrator and the pkg.yeaft.com registry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
